entry.title: Time-Domain Data-Driven Loewner Reduced-Order Models for Electromagnetic Simulation
entry.summary: This paper presents a data-driven Loewner framework for constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) from time-domain electromagnetic (EM) simulation data. High-fidelity simulation of microwave devices can be computationally expensive, particularly when fine spatial discretization and long observation windows are required. The proposed method uses transient input-output data to construct Loewner and shifted Loewner matrices, from which a reduced descriptor realization is obtained through singular value decomposition (SVD). The resulting models are identified from a limited training window and used to predict responses over substantially longer time intervals, with prediction windows up to 50 times the duration of the training window. The method is formalized as an explicit, reproducible algorithm and validated against full-order simulations for four microwave structures: a substrate-integrated-waveguide filter, a frequency-selective surface, an evanescent-mode coaxial comb-line filter, and a diplexer. The results demonstrate the potential of Loewner-based identification to provide compact models of electromagnetic responses while reducing the need for repeated full-order simulation.

entry.title: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
entry.summary: Implicit discretizations of transient heat conduction repeatedly generate sparse linear systems, making diffusion problems a natural test bed for quantum linear solvers. This study evaluates how accurately a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) recovers the temperature field produced by one backward-Euler step of one-dimensional conduction on IBM quantum hardware. A pre-specified confirmatory experiment compares N=4 interior temperatures encoded on two qubits with N=8 temperatures encoded on three qubits using ten paired hardware blocks; a separately defined N=16, four-qubit extension is evaluated in five independently scheduled exploratory blocks. Local VQLS optimization reduces relative temperature-field error to approximately 10^{-8} for all three cases, establishing an essentially exact ideal reference at this scale. On hardware, mean relative L2 temperature-field error is 8.07% for N=4 and 20.14% for N=8, a paired increase of 12.06 percentage points (95% CI, 10.71-13.42; exact paired sign-flip p=0.001953). The exploratory N=16 mean is 24.75+/-1.84%. A pre-specified N=16 shot-count follow-up then evaluates the same locked circuit at 2,048, 8,192, and 32,768 shots in six independently scheduled blocks. Mean field error remains 23.64%, 24.57%, and 24.37%, respectively; the 32,768-minus-2,048-shot contrast is +0.74 percentage points (95% CI, -0.65 to 2.12; p=0.281). In contrast, ideal multinomial sampling predicts a reduction from 2.68% to 0.75%. Higher shot counts reduce block-to-block variability but do not recover the mean cold-side temperature field. The results show that full-field readout of a strongly nonuniform thermal state is limited by more than ordinary finite-shot sampling under the tested hardware conditions, motivating observable-focused quantum formulations for heat flux, stored energy, and selected temperatures.

entry.title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
entry.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training. To address this issue, we propose a modified PI-DeepONet architecture that reduces this cost by removing redundancy in how the Branch network processes input functions across collocation points. The proposed formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original architecture but reduces input tensor sizes and the number of Branch network evaluations. We analyse the computational complexity of both architectures and derive theoretical scaling laws for training time with respect to the number of collocation points and input functions. The proposed architecture is evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection problems. In all cases, it achieves comparable predictive accuracy to the original PI-DeepONet while consistently reducing training time. In 2D experiments, a maximum speed-up of $3.75\times$ is observed, with empirical training-time scaling agreeing with the predicted linear dependence on collocation points and input functions. Furthermore, training a 3D model on an NVIDIA A100 GPU is only feasible using the proposed architecture, as the original formulation exceeds memory limits. These results demonstrate that careful consideration of how PI-DeepONets are implemented can yield substantial gains, enhancing the practical performance of PI-DeepONets and enabling their application to otherwise intractable physics-informed learning problems.

entry.title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
entry.summary: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. Across six three-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU. It also supports zero-shot super-resolution and efficient closed-form spatial derivatives. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29.2-million-node MAST-U tokamak model.

entry.title: Ordinal-pattern transition networks as a symbolic substrate for reservoir computing
entry.summary: Reservoir computing has established itself as a computationally efficient alternative to fully trained recurrent neural networks using a fixed high-dimensional nonlinear substrate to map temporal input into a feature space for a simple readout. Here, we argue that reservoir computing can be realized entirely within a coarse-grained, symbolic state space, and that constrained random walks on ordinal-pattern transition networks provide a natural instance of this realization, replacing the reservoir's continuous state space with a discrete and directly data-derived one. We develop a formal correspondence between the two frameworks, show that the echo-state property has a natural discrete analog in the ergodicity and spectral gap of the walk's underlying Markov chain, and illustrate the correspondence with a minimal example and an empirical one-step-ahead prediction task evaluated across five paradigmatic model systems. These systems exhibit dynamics that correspond to strictly periodic, quasiperiodic, chaotic, or stochastic signals. We argue that this symbolic reservoir perspective allows a redefinition of the reservoir substrate itself, replacing the requirement of a continuous, randomly generated dynamical system with any sufficiently ergodic, data-derived symbolic process. This opens a route toward interpretable, data-adaptive reservoirs whose internal structure is inferred rather than randomly assigned, with implications for surrogate-data methods and reservoir design more broadly.

entry.title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
entry.summary: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.

entry.title: Lossy Lorentz boosts at ultra-relativistic energies: Numerical study and source survey of high-energy physics software
entry.summary: Most high-energy-physics software packages implement Lorentz boosts for themselves. At sufficiently large boosts, these routines can return finite, plausible-looking four-vectors whose invariant masses and rest-frame properties are no longer accurate. We survey implementations in widely used collider and air-shower software and compare representative algorithms in three numerical tests. We find that the main problem is usually information discarded by the representation, rather than the arithmetic of the boost formula. Information can be lost when a boost is specified only by its velocity, and again when the result is stored only through Cartesian components. Richer boost input prevents the first loss, while retaining light-cone coordinates prevents the second. Ordinary hard processes at present colliders are safe in double precision; the relevant regimes are low-mass systems, highly boosted auxiliary frames, single-precision particle records and air-shower simulations. Extreme scale hierarchies in parton-shower accuracy tests and ultra-heavy particle decays provide still more demanding cases.

entry.title: Thermal Confinement in Plasmonic Nanoparticles under Generalised Pulsed Illumination
entry.summary: Thermal confinement is a key parameter in photothermal applications, as it determines the spatial extent of the region affected by the generated heat. In this work, we develop a numerical treatment to quantify thermal confinement in spherical plasmonic nanoparticles under excitation conditions ranging from ultrashort pulses to the continuous-wave regime. The model combines generalized optical heating with a finite-difference solution of the transient heat equation and explicitly accounts for finite interfacial thermal conductance. To characterize the spatial distribution of heat, we introduce a thermal confinement radius defined from the temporal temperature envelope in the surrounding medium. We demonstrate that pulse duration acts as a highly effective, tuneable parameter to govern thermal confinement. Notably, we quantitatively show that finite interfacial thermal conductance can induce deviations of up to 20% in the spatial confinement radius and over 60% in the transient thermal construct under ultrashort excitation. By comparing the characteristic dimensions of representative targeting ligands with the resulting thermal-confinement length scales, we show how pulse duration can be precisely tailored to control target heating. These results provide a unified framework for predicting nanoscale heat localization paving the way for the rational design of high precision thermoplasmonic applications.

entry.title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
entry.summary: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.

entry.title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator for coupled surrogate morphodynamic modelling
entry.summary: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.

entry.title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
entry.summary: We present a closed-form construction of the orbital coefficients of fractional parentage (CFP) of three identical particles in the translationally invariant harmonic oscillator (HO) Jacobi basis. These are usually obtained by numerically diagonalizing a permutation operator in every energy-angular-momentum block. We show this diagonalization is unnecessary. Dressing the class operator $P_{13} + P_{23}$ with the single unitary $W = H^1 Φ$ -- a fixed complexification followed by the HO bracket with mass parameter $d=1$ -- turns it into the label swap times an integer. Every CFP is then the single ket $|K_{i,s}\rangle = 2Q^s W^\dagger|i\rangle$ -- a 2-scaled, sign-decorated column of the $d=1$ bracket restricted to one $e_2$-parity of the labels -- whose norm, $1 + s\langle i | J | i \rangle$, is itself a single matrix element. The same $W$ carries label parity into swap symmetry, $W Q^s W^\dagger = R^s$, making the bookkeeping collapse. The eigenvalues are exact integers $\pm 2$ and $\pm 1$ labeling the $S(3)$ symmetry classes. The construction is uniform in $E$, $L$ and symmetry class, reducing CFP-specific work from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$ in block dimension. An eigensolver remains only inside the bracket engine supplying $H^1$, where all residual numerical error originates. We implement this on an SU(3)-basis bracket engine, checking all 1301 blocks up to $E=50$ (912 366 CFPs, largest block $2907 \times 2907$): the $S(3)$ class assignment is exact everywhere. The residual numerical error (entirely the bracket engine's) stays below $10^{-8}$ for $E \leq 35$, restoring to $\leq 10^{-22}$ via a quadruple-precision build beyond that. We further validate against independently generated antisymmetrization data of a production three-nucleon code, including the $^3$He ground-state energy.

entry.title: RAT-EC: Introducing a New Open-Source 3D Volume-Integral Eddy-Current Module
entry.summary: We present RAT-EC, an open-source volume-integral eddy-current module for unstructured meshes, driven in the time domain by coils of arbitrary winding geometry. It is the first openly available code of this kind and part of the open-source RAT suite. Because only the conductor is meshed, neither the surrounding air nor an artificial outer boundary has to be modelled, which simplifies model preparation and brings problems with thin gaps and intricate air regions within reach of standard hardware. The formulation combines a semi-analytical evaluation of the singular and near-singular inductance terms, a multi-level fast multipole method that accelerates both the far-field inductance action and the coil field, topology-aware constraints for multiply connected conductors, and a matrix-free, GPU-accelerated time integration. The implementation is verified against closed-form solutions for a conducting sphere and a conducting ring, and is validated on the TEAM-7 benchmark. At 50 Hz, RAT-EC reproduces the measured field as accurately as finite-element solutions. At 200 Hz, it agrees with a converged finite-element model, but both deviate from published measurements, which suggests that this benchmark point should be re-examined. RAT-EC provides an open platform for volume-integral eddy-current simulation and method development.

entry.title: A Scalable Sharp-Interface Immersed Boundary Method for Moving Boundary Flow Simulation on Multi-GPU Systems
entry.summary: Sharp-interface immersed boundary methods provide a versatile framework for simulating flows with complex moving boundaries, but their irregular data structures, dynamic sparsity, and discontinuous pressure operators present significant challenges for efficient multi-GPU implementation. This work presents a fully GPU-native, multi-GPU acceleration of the sharp-interface immersed boundary solver, ViCar3D. The implementation combines a hybrid OpenACC/CUDA programming model with a matrix decomposition that isolates dynamically changing immersed-boundary operators, GPU-optimized geometric kernels, asynchronous dual-stream sparse matrix--vector execution, and a symmetric-memory-based sparse communication strategy. A GPU-oriented iterative solver employing a preconditioned stabilized bi-conjugate gradient (BiCGStab) method is developed to efficiently treat the pressure Poisson equation on highly stretched Cartesian grids. The resulting framework preserves the accuracy and versatility of the original solver while delivering substantial acceleration and scalability for simulations involving complex moving and deforming immersed boundaries, thereby extending the applicability of sharp-interface immersed boundary methods to extreme-scale computational fluid dynamics.

entry.title: A differentiable PCA-GPR surrogate framework for full-transient Bayesian inverse uncertainty quantification of black-box nuclear thermal-hydraulic systems
entry.summary: Complex transient energy systems require uncertainty-quantified predictions, but Bayesian inverse uncertainty quantification (IUQ) is often impractical because posterior sampling with high-fidelity system codes requires many expensive full-transient simulations. This study develops a surrogate-assisted Bayesian IUQ framework that makes full-time-series calibration practical for the NACIE heavy-liquid-metal natural-circulation loop. The key innovation is to transform a black-box transient simulator into a differentiable probabilistic emulator by combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression (PCA--GPR). The surrogate reconstructs complete multichannel temperature and mass-flow histories from a compact latent representation, preserving dominant temporal and cross-channel correlations while enabling automatic differentiation of the log posterior. This allows both gradient-free ensemble slice sampling and gradient-informed sampling with the No-U-Turn Sampler and Microcanonical Langevin Monte Carlo. Five principal components capture more than 99\% of the output variance, and the surrogate achieves normalized root-mean-square errors below 2\%. Compared with direct Flownex SE evaluations, the surrogate reduces likelihood-evaluation cost by approximately 3000-fold while preserving posterior statistics and correlations. Posterior predictive analyses show reduced bias, narrower intervals, and improved agreement with measurements and independent validation.

entry.title: Analytically Benchmarked Spatial and Temporal Discretization Guidelines for Finite Element Simulation of Thermal Waves
entry.summary: Finite element simulation is widely used to design and interpret thermal wave-based measurement systems. The accuracy of the results obtained from such simulations depends on how finely the model is resolved in space and time. The discretization resolution is often chosen case by case rather than following a well-defined guideline. This work recommends a discretization protocol for finite element simulation of thermal waves where the spatial discretization is scaled to the thermal diffusion length and the temporal discretization to the number of time steps per cycle. The associated discretization errors are quantified using three benchmark problems of increasing complexity. The spatial phase error converges at second order in the element size, reaching 0.14 degrees at ten elements per diffusion length, whereas the temporal error decreases only at first order in the number of time steps per cycle; thus, the time step can be set from a target phase tolerance $ε$. Each error is assessed against a reference that isolates it. The benchmark case with subsurface defects shows the consequence of violating the recommended discretization protocol.

entry.title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
entry.summary: We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. This treatment accommodates non-Gaussian source spectra and provides inputs for detector specific analyses. A complementary analytical module estimates coupling sensitivities, arrival time delays and screening thresholds from parameterized source and detector properties.

entry.title: Structural identification in general crystalline systems via Voronoi cell topology
entry.summary: Widely used methods for identifying crystal structure in atomistic simulations are limited in practice to a handful of simple structures, leaving many important crystalline systems without automated classification techniques. Voronoi topology analysis offers a route to classifying arbitrary crystalline and defect environments, but realizing this potential first requires enumerating the Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under thermal perturbation of a structure of interest. We present an algorithm that deterministically enumerates all Voronoi cell topologies arising from generic infinitesimal perturbations of an arbitrary crystal structure, producing structural classifiers that extend automated identification to general crystalline systems. We demonstrate the approach on several structures of general interest.
entry.arxiv:comment: 34 pages, 8 figures, 11-page appendix, 18 pages of supplementary material

entry.title: LAO+: Focused, Multi-Replica Accelerated Orthogonal Sampling for Robust Binding Free Energy Predictions
entry.summary: We introduce Lambda-ABF-OPES+ ($\text{LAO+}$), a multi-replica framework for absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations that accelerates both the alchemical transformation and the slow ``orthogonal'' motions coupled to it. At the core of $\text{LAO+}$ is a partitioned $λ$-dynamics scheme that concentrates sampling on the abrupt rehydration of the binding pocket, the main bottleneck of ligand decoupling, while Hamiltonian replica exchange relays configurations along the entire alchemical path. This drives a fourfold gain in convergence speed for the rate-limiting leg over our previous $\text{LAO}$ method, which was itself up to ninefold faster than Lambda-ABF, an overall gain of up to $\sim$36-fold. Applied to 28 protein--ligand complexes across five targets, $\text{LAO+}$ achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.83~kcal~mol$^{-1}$ and a correlation of 0.87 with experiment from only 63~ns of sampling per ligand. Moreover, dedicated reservoir replicas accelerate any slow degree of freedom that can be described by a collective variable. We demonstrate this by recovering hidden protein and ligand conformational states, for example in T4 lysozyme, BRD4 and JNK1. Together, these advances make accurate ABFE calculations practical for drug discovery.

entry.title: Effective Graph Neural Representation of Chain Architectures of Block Copolymers Tested by Predicting RPA Instability Limits
entry.summary: Advances in polymer synthesis and computational modeling are expanding the block-copolymer architecture space accessible for phase-behavior design. Machine learning can accelerate this exploration, yet a common representation capable of learning across diverse chain topologies remains lacking. Here, we present a graph neural network (GNN) representation of acyclic AB multiblock architectures, tested by random-phase approximation (RPA) instability prediction. Each chain is represented as a graph, enabling a common model to learn across diverse topologies. This representation, which organizes RPA-related information, retains predictive capability when extrapolated to architectures with more blocks and demonstrates its potential for reuse across tasks through transfer to instability-wavenumber prediction. By effectively linking block-copolymer chain architecture to field-theoretic response, this graph representation not only reconstructs stability-limit curves but also provides a practical route for future self-consistent field theory exploration of ordered phase space across complex topologies.

entry.title: Learning to reconstruct Germano Differential Filtered Fields with Convolutional Neural Networks for Large Eddy Simulation of Plasma Turbulence
entry.summary: We present a novel method which combines the invertibility of the differential filter of Germano, with convolutional networks to accelerate plasma turbulence simulations. Rather than learning the mapping from coarse-grid LES fields to fine-grid DNS, the proposed method learns the mapping from coarse LES fields to the differential-filtered DNS fields. We then use the inverse of Germano's filter to reconstruct the fine-scale details and hence calculate exactly the nonlinear terms in the governing equations and subgrid-scale terms in the LES equations. The method is tested on the 2D Hasegawa-Wakatani (HW) and modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (mHW) plasma turbulence models at $256^2$ and $512^2$ DNS resolutions using 2, 4 and 8 times smaller LES grids in each direction. We compare the model with DNS results on energy, enstrophy, spectra, probability distributions, poloidal and radial fluxes and computational cost. Validation extends to 1000 simulation time units for HW and 100 for mHW, whose faster dynamics lead toward laminarization. For the $256^2$ cases, the finer LES meshes preserve several integral and spectral features, whereas the coarsest mesh yields unphysical behavior. In contrast, for the $512^2$ cases, even the coarsest LES mesh preserves the turbulent character of the flow and maintains acceptable statistics for both the HW and mHW models. Moreover, we show how our methodology is superior to traditional algebraic numerical LES models, which traditionally fail to capture important design features. Finally, benchmarks show an MPI task-time reductions of 4.82--49.45, with a maximum wall-clock speedup of $1.55\times$ when compared to full CPU socket.

entry.title: Online reduced-order modeling from primal solver trajectories for PDE-constrained optimization
entry.summary: Repeated high-fidelity state and gradient evaluations make large-scale PDE-constrained optimization computationally expensive. Reduced-order modeling provides a natural way to reduce the cost of these repeated high-dimensional computations. However, existing reduced-order modeling approaches often rely on converged high-fidelity states for model construction or updating, while their reduced spaces may lose accuracy as the design moves beyond the region represented by the available data. To address these limitations, we present Reduced-order Trajectory-based Optimization (RETO), an online framework that constructs local reduced-order models (ROMs) directly from unconverged primal solver trajectories. Each local ROM is built from snapshots collected during a finite number of high-fidelity primal iterations, without requiring full-order convergence, and supports multiple low-cost state evaluations, adjoint-based gradient evaluations, and design updates. New solver trajectories are generated at updated design points to reconstruct the local ROM and continue the optimization. Across three distinct PDE-constrained optimization problems, RETO achieves solution quality comparable to that of full-order optimization, with speedups of approximately 8 to 22 times in cases without discontinuities in the state fields. Even in the transonic inverse-design case involving moving shocks, RETO retains an approximately threefold speedup. The transonic results further show that the online local ROM progressively captures evolving shock-related flow features as new primal solver trajectories are incorporated. These results demonstrate the value of unconverged primal solver trajectories as an online information source for reduced-order optimization, allowing the reduced basis to evolve with the design rather than requiring a basis that covers the entire design space in advance.

entry.title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
entry.summary: Rapid prediction of pressure-driven flow in microfluidic porous media is important for experimental design, tracer-test interpretation, and digital-twin development for subsurface energy and critical mineral applications. High-fidelity simulations resolve geometry-controlled flow but are computationally expensive across large geometry ensembles. Here, we introduce GeONet, a Geometry-Encoded Operator Network that predicts steady-state pressure fields by jointly representing material properties, spatial coordinates, and solid--void geometry. GeONet extends the Branch--Trunk architecture with a dedicated Leaf Network encoding the binary domain mask through multiscale features. The Branch Network represents porosity and permeability, the Trunk Network combines coordinates with local geometric descriptors and random Fourier features, and a gated DeepMixer integrates these representations to predict pressure. GeONet was trained and evaluated using 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations of heterogeneous Reduced Complexity Platform domains, comprising nearly 30 TB of data. Comparisons with pore-scale Stokes solutions across three geometries yielded Pearson correlations of 0.987--0.991 and $R^2$ values of 0.974--0.982, supporting PFLOTRAN as reference data. Under matched partitions and two-stage hyperparameter optimization, GeONet substantially outperformed a boundary-condition-aware DeepONet baseline. Across three held-out domains, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381--0.0500, MAPE of 1.76--2.59%, and $R^2$ of 0.9673--0.9822, versus 0.1483--0.2040, 7.81--10.45%, and 0.5658--0.7126 for DeepONet, respectively. On three additional unseen geometries, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0448--0.0676 and $R^2$ of 0.9511--0.9770. These results demonstrate improved accuracy, pressure-range preservation, and cross-geometry generalization through explicit geometry encoding.

entry.title: A nonequilibrium-capturing unified gas-kinetic scheme I: discrete orthogonal basis construction and expansion on velocity space
entry.summary: Velocity space discretization is a primary source of computational cost in deterministic methods for multiscale gas flows. A fixed velocity grid often retains redundant kinetic degrees of freedom (DOFs), particularly under near equilibrium conditions. To address this issue, this work develops a nonequilibrium-capturing formulation based on the unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS), in which the number of kinetic DOFs adapts locally to the degree of nonequilibrium. A discrete orthogonal basis is constructed for numerical implementation, and the velocity distribution function is decomposed into an analytical local equilibrium and a basis expanded nonequilibrium component. The retained, locally adapted DOFs are evolved directly, substantially lowering computational overhead while preserving the discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as accurately capturing nonequilibrium states. The formulation retains the core multiscale coupling of molecular transport and collision inherent to UGKS, providing explicit and implicit schemes for unsteady and steady flows, respectively. Numerical tests across a wide range of flow speeds and rarefaction regimes (from continuum to highly rarefied) demonstrate close agreement with benchmark solutions. For unsteady flows, the explicit scheme achieves speedups of 12.64 to 58.50 over the standard UGKS. In steady state tests, only about $2\%$ of the original kinetic DOFs are required in continuum regions, accelerating each implicit iteration by a factor of 33.87. Even in the most rarefied cases, the scheme captures nonequilibrium behavior using only about $27\%$ of the original DOFs.

entry.title: An implicit multiscale solver for steady kinetic equations based on wave-particle decomposition
entry.summary: Steady kinetic computations require accurate transport on meshes that do not resolve the mean free path and efficient removal of slowly decaying macroscopic errors. We develop a closed wave-particle decomposition (WPD) and a residual-based implicit solver for this problem. The wave accumulates only the Maxwellian along a local characteristic horizon and is determined by the conservative variables; the particle carries the kinetic complement and collision remainder. Under moment compatibility, the closed system is equivalent to the kinetic equation. For the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and Shakhov models, a hydrodynamic expansion gives the wave and particle contributions to the Euler and Navier-Stokes fluxes. The implicit iteration couples macroscopic prediction to microscopic correction through a discrete endpoint term and synchronizes the conservative moments after each accepted correction. Its stationary states satisfy the target discrete kinetic equation independently of the iteration controls. Formal analysis gives the smooth fixed-mesh fluid limit. Linear model analysis relates convergence to the horizon-to-relaxation ratio, incomplete macroscopic solves and explicit collision remainders. One- and two-dimensional computations of a normal shock, internal flows and hypersonic external flows test these properties across rarefied and continuum regimes. The results show kinetic fidelity and substantial reductions in iteration counts and wall time relative to the conventional iterative scheme near the continuum limit. Collision-model comparisons and parameter studies support the predicted convergence mechanisms.

entry.title: Standardized Planck-Mean Absorption Coefficients for High-Temperature Gases
entry.summary: Planck-mean absorption coefficients of pure gases are calculated from line-by-line integrations of HITEMP and ExoMol spectra up to 5000 K for use in high-enthalpy radiative heat transfer simulations. The dataset extends beyond conventional combustion products, including high-temperature radicals, nitrogen-bearing species, soot precursors, metal oxides, metal hydrides, and halides: AlF, AlH, AlO, BH, C2, C2H2, CH, CH4, CN, CO, CO2, H2O, HBO, HCN, HF, MgH, MgO, N2O, NO, NO2, OH, SiO, TiH, TiO. New calculations are validated against historical correlations for overlapping species, demonstrating good agreement over their applicable temperature ranges. Strong visible opacities result in large Planck-mean absorption coefficients for many of the considered species, highlighting the need to account for their radiative contribution in extreme environments. A brute-force search over several candidate functional forms is performed to provide a common set of coefficients, establishing a standardized framework that can be easily integrated into production solvers and extended as additional high-temperature line lists become available.

entry.title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
entry.summary: This work extends the Deep Energy Method to phase-field modelling of ductile fracture in elasto-plastic solids. Its key contribution is an incremental DEM-based formulation that couples history-dependent J2 plasticity and plasticity-dependent fracture toughness with separate energy-optimised displacement and phase-field representations. The formulation combines the second-order Ambrosio-Tortorelli phase-field fracture model with small-strain J2 plasticity and linear isotropic hardening. A volumetric-deviatoric split defines the elastic crack-driving energy, while accumulated equivalent plastic strain governs the degradation of local fracture toughness. Plastic internal variables are updated locally through radial return. The reduced energy is minimised alternately with respect to the displacement and phase fields, represented by a ReZero residual neural network and spatially localised Gaussian radial basis functions with trainable centres, respectively. This split addresses the diffuse phase-field profiles observed in preliminary calculations with a shared global network. Alternating optimisation is combined with transfer learning to reuse trainable parameters and optimiser states across loading increments, while the converged constitutive history is carried forward separately at quadrature points. The numerical results demonstrate close agreement with finite-element reference solutions in predicting force-displacement responses, energy evolution, plastic deformation and crack propagation. The framework captures the main features of ductile fracture, although accuracy becomes more sensitive to loading increments near abrupt fracture events.

entry.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
entry.summary: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.

entry.title: A Transferable Machine-Learned Potential Enabling Large-Scale Copper-Carbon Simulations from Equilibrium to Extreme Conditions
entry.summary: Cu-C materials and interfaces are central to diamond thermal management, metallization, graphene growth and carbon-coating technologies, but atomistic simulations across these applications require a potential that describes metallic Cu, diverse carbon bonding, heterogeneous Cu-C interactions and close atomic encounters. Here we develop NEP-CuC, a transferable neuroevolution potential trained on a dataset of 2,727 uniformly relabelled configurations selected from a heterogeneous Cu-C candidate pool. Disagreement within an ensemble of five independently trained models provides an internal indicator of model sensitivity. A Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark (ZBL) correction describes short-range nuclear repulsion, while a runtime D3(BJ) correction supplements dispersion-sensitive calculations. Tests on source-derived held-out and independent external datasets, together with structural, elastic, defect, interfacial, vibrational and finite-temperature transport benchmarks, establish broad but property-dependent physical fidelity across elemental Cu, diverse carbon environments and heterogeneous Cu-C configurations. Large-scale simulations of amorphous-carbon formation and orientation-dependent shock compression of Cu further test transferability under strongly non-equilibrium conditions. For Cu/diamond interfaces, the same potential describes deposition, annealing and tensile response: preparation history leaves persistent differences in interphase structure, while the mean peak nominal tensile stress at 500 K decreases from $12.35\pm0.71$ to $6.65\pm0.98$ GPa as the incident Cu energy during the initial deposition stage increases from 1 to 50 eV. NEP-CuC provides an atomistic framework for linking processing, interfacial structure and physical response across Cu-C systems, with direct relevance to Cu/diamond thermal-management interfaces, diamond metallization and non-equilibrium Cu-C processing.

entry.title: A quantum-assisted latent surrogate model for Bayesian inversion of heterogeneous material properties on NISQ hardware
entry.summary: Bayesian inversion is widely used in engineering applications, including material characterisation, structural damage identification, and medical diagnostics. These inverse problems are typically ill-posed, because localised variations in material properties must be inferred from noisy observations, and they are computationally intensive, since they often require many evaluations of a high-fidelity forward solver. Quantum computing has recently attracted considerable interest, partly because some near-term algorithms are feasible on NISQ hardware. In particular, PQC combined with classical optimisation enable a hybrid quantum-classical surrogate model. A central obstacle to applying such circuits to inversion is that the discretised parameter and response fields are far too high-dimensional to be embedded in a near-term quantum register. In this work we propose a quantum-assisted latent surrogate model for the Bayesian inversion of inhomogeneous material properties, in which latent compression bridges these high-dimensional fields and the small registers accessible to near-term circuits. The low intrinsic dimensional structure of the spatially varying conductivity and potential fields is exploited by reducing the conductivity through PCA and the response through a convolutional autoencoder. A PQC is then trained to map the latent conductivity to the latent response, and stochastic variational inference is performed entirely in latent space. The methodology is demonstrated on one- and two-dimensional inverse problems under both informative and non-informative priors. We further evaluate the model on IonQ simulator and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q, and use a lightweight learned denoising stage that recovers the noiseless accuracy to within a small residual. (The abstract has been shortened to meet arXiv's 1,920-character limit. For the full Abstract, please download the full Article.)

entry.title: A Topological Spin on Racetrack Memory: Stability and Transport of 360° Domain Walls in Magnetic Nanotubes
entry.summary: Magnetic racetrack memory requires localized carriers that combine rapid motion, resistance to perturbations and a detectable signal. Here we show how a 360° domain wall in a hollow ferromagnetic tube combines these properties within a single continuous magnetic shell. Two successive magnetization reversals form a bound object whose surrounding domains point in the same direction. Analytical energetics and micromagnetic simulations establish its finite separation, recovery from tested perturbations and current driven transport without microscopic Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction or a maintaining field. The texture's winding resists unwinding while radial rotation carries an energy cost, providing a specific control over stability. Relative rotation of the constituent spins accounts quantitatively for additional displacement during current onset. The wall supports motion at hundreds of metres per second, with transient velocities approaching one kilometre per second at stronger drive. A prepared seven-bit pattern retains its carriers and local readout contrast after pulsed transport and recovery. Curved-track and differential-current tests identify radial stiffness and drive uniformity as controls for intact motion. These results establish a physical basis for fast, locally distinguishable tubular magnetic bits and identify a continuous switching pathway that can be targeted by tailored excitation.

entry.title: Advanced computational methods for simulating the classical hydrogen atom in stochastic electrodynamics
entry.summary: Stochastic electrodynamics (SED) is a theory of nature that seeks to derive key aspects of quantum mechanics and quantum electrodynamics from a purely classical physics perspective. While SED has been successful in many areas, it has largely failed to stably simulate the 3D classical hydrogen atom. The computational methodology presented here overcomes these foundational challenges. We develop a pseudo-wave formulation that integrates the solid angle in k-space utilizing symmetry, resulting in a significantly reduced memory footprint and lower computational overhead for generating the zero-point radiation spectrum. This optimization is paired with a logarithmic frequency grid, a sliding window tracking the instantaneous Keplerian frequency, and a Tukey smoothing function to eliminate discrete force discontinuities. Integrated via an adaptive RKF45 solver across highly dense grids of up to 100-million bins, these techniques demonstrate the asymptotic convergence of ensemble stability. We show that increasing the grid resolution in the high-frequency domain systematically mitigates artificial electron decay, yielding a simulated probability density function that closely aligns with the quantum mechanical ground state P(r).

entry.title: Local-resolvent formulation and assessment of linear-scaling Kohn-Sham calculations
entry.summary: Kohn-Sham density-functional theory is expensive because it needs orbitals that extend over the whole system. For insulators this can be avoided by using only the diagonal of the one-electron resolvent, $g(\mathbf{r},z)=\langle\mathbf{r}|(z-\hat h)^{-1}|\mathbf{r}\rangle$, at a few complex energies $z$. We call the scheme local-resolvent density-functional theory (LRes-DFT). The density and the band energy are linear in $g$, so neither orbitals nor a kinetic-energy functional are needed. The complex energies are $M$ equally spaced points on a circle that encloses the occupied levels, offset by half a spacing so that no point lies on the real axis. Summing the resolvent over them is equivalent to occupying each level with $1/(1+u^M)$, where $u$ is the level's energy measured from the circle's center in units of its radius. This is a smooth step that is near 1 inside the circle and near 0 outside, and it stays between 0 and 1 for every $M$. If the circle moves with the chemical potential, forces at fixed electron number are exact. Gauss-Legendre and Zolotarev rules need fewer points when the gap is small. In three dimensions we use eigenpairs of small windows around each molecule instead of resolvents. This is divide-and-conquer (DC) with a different occupation function, and it is as accurate as DC with Fermi-Dirac occupations. For H$_2$ molecular crystals of up to 1024 electrons it agrees with Kohn-Sham to $2.5\times10^{-7}$ Ha per electron. On one core it is slower than dense diagonalization below about 500 electrons and 3.5 times faster at 1024 electrons. It loses accuracy for disordered or compressed systems and for diffuse basis functions.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Bell-Shaped Gaussian Quadratures in Deterministic Boltzmann Solvers
entry.summary: In this work, we develop a unified theoretical framework that constructs Bell-shaped Gaussian quadratures for deterministic Boltzmann solvers. The proposed framework establishes a general class of bell-shaped weight functions together with the corresponding integral transformations, revealing the common mathematical structure underlying existing generalized Gaussian quadratures. Based on this framework, a unified procedure for constructing discrete velocity sets is developed by combining radial quadratures with appropriate directional quadratures in different velocity-space dimensions. Several existing generalized Gaussian quadratures are naturally recovered as special cases, while the proposed framework provides a systematic route for constructing new quadrature rules based on different bell-shaped weight functions. Extensive benchmark simulations over a broad range of flow regimes demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high integration accuracy and computational efficiency with significantly fewer discrete velocities than conventional quadrature strategies. Overall, the proposed framework not only unifies existing generalized Gaussian quadratures under a common mathematical foundation but also establishes a general design principle for the systematic development of efficient velocity-space quadratures in deterministic Boltzmann solvers.

entry.title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?
entry.summary: Although machine learning potentials (MLPs) generalize across configurational and chemical compound spaces, their accuracy is commonly believed to be limited by their training methods, with improvements beyond this limit achieved so far only by refitting to experimental observables. In this Perspective, we argue that MLPs can also be made more accurate than their training methods non-empirically by generalizing across a third space, that of quantum-chemical methods. We propose routes to method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods, with working implementations in both density-functional and wavefunction-based theories showing that they can be more accurate than any of their training methods. Aiming beyond the accuracy of the training methods could also make universal MLPs more accurate than single-method models, even when the method-transferable MLPs remain less accurate than those QM methods. Method-transferable MLPs will shape the construction of training datasets and the evaluation of models, pushing the accuracy limits of chemical simulations.

entry.title: All-electron machine-learned orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems
entry.summary: We introduce STRUCTURES-P, a machine-learned all-electron orbital-free density functional for periodic CHNO systems. Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

entry.title: Simultaneous energy and entropy stability of volume-penalisation immersed-boundary methods for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations
entry.summary: Immersed-boundary methods avoid body-fitted meshes, but the energy or entropy stability of the underlying flow discretisation does not automatically extend to the immersed treatment. This manuscript analyses the volume-penalised compressible Navier--Stokes equations for both energy and entropy stability, on the continuous and semi-discrete levels, and integrates the isolated source exactly in time. The source is formulated as a one-parameter family indexed by $θ$, whose momentum component relaxes the fluid velocity towards the prescribed solid velocity; $θ$ sets how much of the resulting kinetic-energy loss leaves the domain rather than being converted to internal energy. The two stability requirements impose opposing bounds on $θ$, with dissipation of the relative total energy requiring $θ\geq0$ and stability of the mathematical entropy requiring $θ\leq1$. Where penalisation acts, both conditions are therefore satisfied if and only if $0\leqθ\leq1$, and the symmetric value $θ=1/2$ divides the kinetic-energy loss equally between the domain and the internal energy. We conclude that any entropy-stable split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method remains semi-discretely entropy stable once the source is added at the collocation nodes, for stationary and prescribed moving bodies alike.

entry.title: WannierSTM: Efficient superconducting scanning-probe spectroscopy from maximally localized Wannier functions
entry.summary: We present a Python-based program that combines maximally localized Wannier functions-based first-principles electronic structure with the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism to enable efficient simulations of scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The workflow builds upon standard density functional theory packages to construct compact transport Hamiltonians that preserve the properties of realistic materials. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential within the Nambu-spinor formalism, while coupling to the STM tip and substrate electrodes is treated using the wide-band limit approximation. Within this formulation, transport quantities such as current-voltage characteristics and differential conductance are evaluated in a closed analytical form. This avoids explicit numerical energy integrations and enables rapid spectroscopic calculations over broad parameter spaces. The framework provides a unified and computationally efficient approach for modeling superconducting hybrid nanostructures with spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization. Representative applications in spin chains, two-dimensional and molecular magnets on a superconductor demonstrate its robust capabilities for both simple model systems and realistic ab initio molecular structures relevant to modern STM experiments.

entry.title: Deep Mesoscopic Dynamics
entry.summary: Microscopic simulations resolve spatial patterns but are feasible only over small domains and short timescales, whereas bulk descriptions erase those patterns through spatial averaging. Mesoscopic fields preserve this spatial organisation, but their effective equations are known only for selected microscopic systems and scaling limits. We introduce Deep Mesoscopic Dynamics (DeepMesoD), which uses neural networks to learn an effective mesoscopic field equation from microscopic trajectories at a prescribed coarse-graining scale. For the nonconserved dissipative dynamics studied here, DeepMesoD learns the free-energy functional with a spatial interaction kernel and a state-dependent dissipation operator constrained by the fluctuation-dissipation relation. We first validate the construction in the Ising-Kac model, where the learned mesoscopic equation recovers the known hydrodynamic limit and rollouts remain stable far beyond the training horizon. We then treat two systems without closed-form mesoscopic descriptions. For a two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet governed by atomistic spin dynamics, DeepMesoD learns a mesoscopic model whose predictions match atomistic references up to 1 ns, and a rollout with an unseen initial condition remains bounded up to 25 ns. For layered CrBr$_3$, the learned kernel captures the suppression and sign reversal of interlayer coupling at a stacking fault whose location and strength are not supplied as inputs. Controlled changes to the learned interaction show how fault number and placement shape multistep magnetic responses, complementing our magneto-photoluminescence measurements. Across the two atomistic systems, DeepMesoD achieves a three-to-four-order-of-magnitude reduction in wall-clock time compared with atomistic spin dynamics.

entry.title: Colossal Spin--Lattice--Charge Coupling in Noncollinear Ferrimagnetic NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) Monolayers
entry.summary: Noncollinear ferrimagnets combine a net magnetic moment with internal spin degrees of freedom, creating opportunities to couple magnetic, mechanical, thermal, and electronic responses. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomistic spin simulations, and transport modeling, we identify stable NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) monolayers with noncollinear ferrimagnetic ground states and Curie temperatures up to 313 K. Competing exchange, Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, and magnetic anisotropy produce field-responsive canted states that couple strongly to the lattice and charge carriers. Magnetization rotation changes the elastic modulus of NbMnTe$_2$ by up to 36\%, while lattice entropy substantially enhances the near-room-temperature magnetocaloric response of NbMnS$_2$ and NbMnSe$_2$. In NbMnSe$_2$, rotation restores a mirror-protected crossing, continuously closes an approximately 0.13 eV gap, and produces a conductivity-based anisotropic magnetoresistance ratio up to 10,000\% at 100 K. The combined results establish noncollinear NbMnX$_2$ monolayers as a multifunctional platform for two-dimensional spintronics, nanomechanics, and thermal control.

entry.title: A Parameter-Free Reference Hamiltonian for Tight-Binding Vanadium Oxides
entry.summary: Density-functional tight binding has yet to yield a transferable description of vanadium oxides; for the standard second-order construction and the tested cells, we demonstrate that two of its approximations deviate by electron volts and offset each other in the band-index centroid separation between the V 3d and O 2p bands: the neutral two-centre reference omits electron-volt environmental terms, whereas the Mulliken charge model assigns the compact V 3d shell less than half of the self-consistent potential shift observed in PBE. Instead, we build a tight-binding model where the reference Hamiltonian derives from superposed neutral atoms, the full PBE exchange-correlation potential and frozen-core orthogonality, without adjustable terms, and where the orbital-resolved charge response employs three screening factors obtained from PBE linear response and an unscreened Coulomb range. Relative to the primary PAW reference, the plane-wave Harris-Foulkes energy differences of VO2 are matched by the reference energy at fixed geometry and the stated numerical settings, with signed deviations of +2.6 meV/atom for M1 relative to rutile (an energy difference of 92 meV/atom) and +6.2 and -5.2 meV/atom under 3% volume compression and expansion; the charge response reproduces 14 of 22 fitted and 5 of 8 held-out matched PBE responses within one tolerance, and 28 of the 30 within twice the tolerance, and in rutile the fitted first-radial V 3d shift is -4.39 eV, 0.47 eV more negative than PBE's -3.92 eV, whereas the tested DFTB2 charge model gives -1.53 eV. The convexity of the spinless model at fixed geometry prevents it from spontaneously differentiating symmetry-equivalent sites under the symmetries respected by its implemented operators and sampling, so within this model such differentiation in the Magnéli phases must arise from electron-lattice coupling or an explicit spin or correlation term.

entry.title: A grand potential for molten-salt electrochemical phase diagrams from first principles
entry.summary: The clean-energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for metals, whose extraction is among the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions. Molten-salt electrolysis offers a path toward carbon-free production of aluminum, iron, titanium, and critical metals. However, corrosive operating conditions and complex, multicomponent feedstocks make experimental development costly and challenging. Here, we introduce a first-principles framework for constructing electrochemical phase diagrams of multicomponent systems to accelerate electrode and electrolyte design and guide the selection of compatible materials and operating conditions for electrochemical cells. We derive a grand potential that generates these diagrams at scale, and supply free energies using first-principles data obtained through a fine-tuned foundation machine-learned interatomic potential. For silicon in molten CaCl$_2$, the construction not only recovers the experimental diagram when using the first-principles framework on a limited set of structures, but also predicts further domains when extended to a larger set of crystal structures. Finally, we demonstrate the predictive power of the approach by screening ten alkali and alkaline-earth halide electrolytes for aluminum electrowinning. Three thermodynamic criteria identify NaF, where cryolite emerges as the stable aluminum-bearing phase, recovering the chemistry that Hall and Héroult established empirically in 1886. The framework provides a first-principles basis for selecting compatible electrodes, electrolytes, and operating conditions toward low-carbon metal production from complex source materials.

entry.title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
entry.summary: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. We present convergence scans and benchmarks against the established beam-beam codes GUINEA-PIG (v1.2.2) and CAIN (v2.42) for luminosity spectra, photon emission, and secondary-particle production under a wide range of beam parameters corresponding to different collider concepts. Our results show that WarpX (v26.09) reproduces the benchmark beam-beam observables while enabling GPU-portable, extensible simulations. These results establish WarpX as a scalable platform for high-fidelity beam-beam modeling in future collider studies.

entry.title: Structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics for partial differential equations
entry.summary: Machine learning surrogates of partial differential equations (PDEs) are commonly trained on data generated by numerical solvers. Therefore, the training data obey not the PDE but the modified equation of the numerical scheme, and the test loss, computed on data from the same solver, cannot distinguish a model that learned the physics from one that learned the discretization error. Here, we show that the difference is nevertheless visible in the trained model. We propose a suite of structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics, simple scores that measure whether a learned model respects one known property of the physics, such as a conserved quantity, a symmetry or a Hamiltonian structure, without access to the training data or the governing equation. Over five systems, the diagnostics track the error with respect to the true dynamics with a rank correlation of up to $0.94$, while the test loss is uncorrelated or anti-correlated with it. For the Burgers, Korteweg-de Vries and Navier-Stokes equations, the diagnostics separate numerical schemes that the test loss ranks as equivalent, including schemes of the same order. order.

entry.title: KINTORA: a semi-Lagrangian discontinuous Galerkin drift-kinetic, unstructured mesh tokamak solver
entry.summary: Continuum gyrokinetic codes use structured, field-aligned grids on nested flux surfaces; particle-in-cell codes support unstructured meshes and open field lines but carry a statistical noise floor. We present a continuum drift-kinetic solver that occupies neither position: a semi-Lagrangian discontinuous Galerkin discretization on unstructured triangular poloidal planes extruded toroidally, whose parallel advance is a map along the exact field line in the flux-coordinate independent manner, so the mesh is never aligned with the field, with adiabatic electrons and a long-wavelength polarization field solve. Every operator is verified against an independently computed reference, from Landau damping to the geodesic-acoustic root and a linear ion-temperature-gradient eigenvalue problem, every measured rate within 4% except the geodesic-acoustic damping, within 12%. A linear toroidal ion-temperature-gradient demonstration on a canonical-Maxwellian equilibrium recovers a radially coherent mode whose growth rate, 0.065 c_s/a, is stationary in time. The collisionless zonal-flow residual is the one measurement still moving: it rises with poloidal refinement from 0.72 to 0.87 of the model's own orbit-quadrature prediction for the measured observable and has not converged. The solver is fully device resident, and every result is reproduced between CPU and GPU builds and across MPI process counts. The code, the data behind every table and an artifact description are in a public repository.

entry.title: A Method for Exact Enforcement of Boundary Conditions on General Curved Triangular Domains: Algorithm and Application to Scientific Machine Learning
entry.summary: We present a method for enforcing exactly Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on general triangular domains with arbitrarily curved boundaries. The algorithmic constructions developed here complements those in a previous work for general quadrilateral domains. Our method combines (i) the exact mapping between a general curved triangular domain and the standard triangle, (ii) TFC constrained expressions, and (iii) Barnhill transfinite interpolations, to provide explicit closed-form trial ansatze that mathematically satisfy the imposed boundary conditions exactly. Corner compatibility induced by the boundary conditions is pivotal, and enforcing exactly the imposed boundary conditions hinges on the exact enforcement of the induced compatibility constraints. The corner compatibility associated with the acute vertices of the standard triangle and the coupling between gradient components when the hypotenuse corresponds to a Neumann/Robin boundary pose particular challenges. Two strategies are critical to resolving these issues, by reformulating conditional corner constraints into equivalent unconditional forms and by introducing a separate TFC-style auxiliary edge construction together with an associated linear solve on the hypotenuse. We analyze the corner compatibility constraints and present formulations for the general form of functions that exactly satisfy the imposed Dirichlet, Neumann, or Robin conditions on curved triangular domains. The proposed method has been implemented using extreme learning machine type randomized neural networks for solving PDE problems. We present ample numerical experiments with linear/nonlinear PDE problems on a variety of domains with complex boundary geometries. Numerical results show that the current method has enforced the Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on curved domain boundaries to the machine precision.

entry.title: Wisevolve Potential Engine: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics at 100 Million Atom-Steps per Second on a Single GPU
entry.summary: General-purpose molecular dynamics software supports diverse interatomic potentials and simulation requirements. Within a simulation stage, the loaded potential model and the required calculations typically remain fixed as the atomic configuration evolves. We present the Wisevolve Potential Engine (WPE), which uses this information from GPUMD to select and reuse a GPU execution policy tailored to the model and simulation stage. GPUMD retains simulation control and ownership of the simulation data. On a single NVIDIA RTX 5090, WPE-enabled GPUMD (GPUMD-WPE) achieves a median throughput of 109 million atom-step/s across 106 neuroevolution potential (NEP) workloads. For a 15.1-million-atom diamond Si system, it sustains 142 million atom-step/s. Relative to GPUMD, geometric-mean speedups are 3.49x across these NEP workloads, 3.61x across 16 workloads using NEP with dynamic charges (qNEP), 1.24x across 28 classical-potential workloads, and 10.5x across 56 path-integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) configurations. End-to-end calculations of water structure, lattice thermal conductivity, and PIMD thermal expansion show close agreement with corresponding GPUMD results and published simulation results. A separate 12.5-million-atom Cu shock-compression simulation demonstrates its applicability to large-scale nonequilibrium dynamics. These results support model- and stage-specific specialization as a practical way to accelerate GPU potential evaluation in general-purpose molecular dynamics workflows.

entry.title: Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
entry.summary: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxides. Whether universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs), which lack explicit electronic degrees of freedom, can describe them remains unclear. Here, we investigate H-induced electron localization across a range of TM oxides using a geometric descriptor based on TM-O bond-length expansion (Z-score) to identify polaronic distortions. We find that uMLIPs exhibit varying degrees of electron localization, from delocalized states to metastable small polarons, with their behavior strongly dependent on the training data and treatment of electronic correlations. In particular, the absence of Hubbard U corrections for specific TM cations in the training data leads to electron delocalization, in contrast to DFT+U predictions. Although some uMLIPs reproduce polaron hopping barriers during coupled proton-polaron transfer, all of them fail to stabilize spatially separated polaron-donor configurations, instead favoring localization near the H dopant.
